	# How the spacing works

  ## `sizable` mixin
  
  To make an element able to receive dynamic spacing, you need to include the `sizable{:sass}` mixin in your element's scope. Including the mixin declares three variables: `--is-small{:sass}`, `--is-medium{:sass}`, and `--is-large{:sass}`. Each variable holds a different calculation that determines which of the three sizes: `small`, `medium`, or `large`, is applied to the element. These variables are required in order to switch between the three sizes. 
  
  It’s important to note that only the element where the `sizable{:sass}` mixin is included becomes sizable. Child elements inside it will not automatically inherit this behavior.

  ## `pad()` function

  The `pad(){:js}` function works in the same way as the [sizable()](how-the-sizing-works#sizable-function) function: based on the `--component-size{:sass}` value, one of the three size variables (`--is-small{:sass}`, `--is-medium{:sass}`, and `--is-large{:sass}`) is set to `1`, while the others remain `0`. The `pad(){:js}` function then multiplies these variables by the size values passed as parameters. Since two of them are `0`, only the active size produces a positive result in the calculations. The difference here is that, before the result is applied to the element’s property, it is also multiplied by a spacing factor, `--ig-spacing{:sass}`, which acts as a multiplier for the values passed to the `pad(){:js}` function. We will discuss the multiplier in more detail in the next section about the [Spacing factor](spacing-factor)

  ## `pad-inline()` and `pad-block()` functions

  In addition to the `pad(){:js}` function, there are two additional functions: `pad-inline(){:bash}` and `pad-block(){:bash}`. They can be used to style only the inline padding (left and right) or only the block padding (top and bottom). The two functions work the same way as the `pad(){:js}` function, but they tie the returned size calculations to different multipliers than the default `--ig-spacing{:sass}`.

  - `pad-inline(){:bash}` uses the `--ig-spacing-inline{:sass}` multiplier.

  - `pad-block(){:bash}` uses the `--ig-spacing-block{:sass}` multiplier.

  We highly recommend using the `pad-inline(){:bash}` function only when styling the padding-inline property, and the `pad-block(){:bash}` function only when styling the padding-block property. This ensures that all padding is tied to the correct multipliers and that you are applying padding only where it is needed.

  ```scss
  .wrapper {
    @include sizable();
    padding-inline: pad-inline($sm: 10px, $md: 20px, $lg: 50px); /* [!code highlight] */
    padding-block: pad-block($sm: 10px, $md: 20px, $lg: 50px); /* [!code highlight] */
    --component-size: var(--ig-size-medium);
  }
  ```
